newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka leader in peace appeal on Independence Day.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka leader in peace appeal on Independence Day.

text.p: President Chandrika Kumaratunga, in an Independence Day speech on Tuesday, called on Sri Lankans to put aside differences and work to end a 14-year war between government forces and minority Tamil rebels.
"The promise of lasting peace is in the air," Kumaratunga said in an address to the nation during a ceremony to mark the country's 49th year of independence from Britain.
Kumaratunga said she believed the Indian Ocean island, whose majority people are Sinhalese, had enough space and resources to offer equal opportunities to all its communities.
She spoke first in Sinhalese, then in English. Her speech was also translated into Tamil.

The war has recently been confined to remote parts in the north and east of the island but there is no end in sight to frequent clashes between government forces and guerrillas of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
Security was tight in the capital Colombo for Independence Day celebrations after intelligence reports of possible rebel attacks.
Hundreds of armed policemen and troops were deployed to guard the ceremony held at Independence Square in downtown Colombo. The capital was ringed with numerous checkpoints.
The LTTE is fighting for a separate homeland in north and east Sri Lanka. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict, but the rebels say the toll is higher.

"If we only direct that stupendous commitment of our young people -- who so readily sacrificed their lives at the altar of destruction and divison, towards building bridges of understanding and peace as well as roads, waterways, schools and hospitals, power and communications networks, factories and farms -- we have won the final victory," she said.
The rebels have ignored a peace plan offered in 1995 by Kumaratunga, which would give Tamils limited autonomy in the north and east.
Her government said last week that the offer had been revised and included in a draft constitution that would be announced in the first week of April.
The proposed new constitution must be passed in parliament and then approved in a referendum.
Kumaratunga said her government's achievements in restoring democracy and laying the foundation for a strong economy would remain fragile as long as the ethnic war continued.
On Sunday, police in the eastern port of Trincomalee arrested a suspected member of an LTTE hit squad believed to have been on a mission to kill prominent politicians in Colombo.

The 26-year-old suspect, identified as S. Ravishankar, was suspected of being an accomplice of a woman suicide bomber who killed herself to avoid arrest at a checkpoint in Colombo last week, police said. LTTE rebels wear cyanide suicide capsules around their necks to avoid being captured alive.
The LTTE has not commented on the arrest.
Police are looking for three other women Tamil rebel suicide bombers said to have come into Colombo, police officials said.
